questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Which element from following has positive electron gain enthalpy?
questions.solution:
Electron gain enthalpy is the enthalpy change when an electron is added to a neutral gaseous atom.

Halogens such as Chlorine, Bromine, and Iodine have a strong tendency to accept an electron to achieve a stable noble gas configuration, resulting in highly negative electron gain enthalpies.

Noble gases like Xenon have a completely filled and stable valence shell (ns^2 np^6$). Adding an electron requires energy to place it in a higher energy principal quantum shell, overcoming interelectronic repulsions. Thus, Xenon has a positive electron gain enthalpy.

Answer: Xenon$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Which of the following elements belongs to group 2 and sixth period of periodic table?
questions.solution:
Group 2 elements are alkaline earth metals: Beryllium (Be), Magnesium (Mg), Calcium (Ca), Strontium (Sr), Barium (Ba), and Radium (Ra).

The periods corresponding to these elements are:
Period 2: Beryllium
Period 3: Magnesium
Period 4: Calcium
Period 5: Strontium
Period 6: Barium
Period 7: Radium

Therefore, the element belonging to group 2 and the sixth period is Barium.

Answer: Barium

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Identify increasing order of acidity for following diprotic acids in aqueous solutions.
questions.solution:
The given compounds are hydrides of Group 16 elements.

As we move down the group from Sulphur (S) to Tellurium (Te), the atomic size of the central atom increases.

This leads to an increase in the H-E bond length (where E is S, Se, Te) and a corresponding decrease in the bond dissociation enthalpy.

Consequently, the H-E bond becomes weaker, making the release of an $\textH^{+}$ ion easier.

Therefore, the acidic strength increases down the group.

The increasing order of acidity is $\text{H}_2\text{S} < \text{H}_2\text{Se} < \text{H}_2\text{Te}$.

Answer: $\text{H}_2\text{S} < \text{H}_2\text{Se} < \text{H}_2\text{Te}$

questions.solution:
Astatine (At) is a chemical element with atomic number $85$.

It belongs to the halogen family, which includes Fluorine (F), Chlorine (Cl), Bromine (Br), Iodine (I), Astatine (At), and Tennessine (Ts).

The halogen family is located in Group $17$ of the modern periodic table.

Answer: $17$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: What happens to the size of atoms in p-block elements when we move from left to right in the same period?
questions.solution:
As we move from left to right across a period, the atomic number increases, meaning the number of protons in the nucleus increases.

The additional electrons are added to the same principal shell, so the shielding effect remains almost constant.

This results in an increase in the effective nuclear charge (Z_{eff}$), which pulls the valence electrons closer to the nucleus.

Consequently, the atomic size decreases from left to right in the same period.

Answer: Size decreases$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Which group elements have the smallest atomic radii in their respective periods?
questions.solution:
In a given period, the atomic radius decreases from left to right as the effective nuclear charge increases.

This trend continues up to group 17 (halogens).

For group 18 (noble gases), the atomic radius is expressed as van der Waals radius since they do not form covalent bonds under normal conditions.

Since van der Waals radii are always larger than covalent radii, group 18 elements have larger radii than group 17 elements.

Thus, group 17 elements possess the smallest atomic radii in their respective periods.

Answer: group 17

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Which of the following compounds is most acidic in nature?
questions.solution:
The given compounds are hydrides of Group 16 elements.

As we move down the group from oxygen to tellurium, the atomic size of the central atom increases.

Due to the increase in atomic size, the bond length of the $\text{H-E}$ bond (where $\text{E}$ is $\text{O}$, $\text{S}$, $\text{Se}$, $\text{Te}$) increases, which leads to a decrease in the bond dissociation enthalpy.

A lower bond dissociation enthalpy means the $\text{H-E}$ bond can be broken more easily to release an $\text{H}^+$ ion.

Therefore, the acidic character increases down the group.

The order of acidic strength is $\text{H}_2\text{O} < \text{H}_2\text{S} < \text{H}_2\text{Se} < \text{H}_2\text{Te}$.

Thus, $\text{H}_2\text{Te}$ is the most acidic compound among the given options.

Answer: $\text{H}_2\text{Te}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Which of the following hydrides of Group $16$ elements has highest reducing property?
questions.solution:
The reducing property of Group $16$ hydrides depends on the ease with which they can release hydrogen atoms.

As we move down the group from oxygen to tellurium, the atomic size of the central atom increases.

This leads to an increase in the $E-\text{H}$ bond length ($E = \text{O, S, Se, Te}$) and a corresponding decrease in the bond dissociation enthalpy.

Due to the lowest bond dissociation enthalpy among the given options, $\text{H}_2\text{Te}$ releases hydrogen most easily.

Therefore, the reducing property increases in the order: $\text{H}_2\text{O} < \text{H}_2\text{S} < \text{H}_2\text{Se} < \text{H}_2\text{Te}$.

Hence, $\text{H}_2\text{Te}$ has the highest reducing property.

Answer: $\text{H}_2\text{Te}$

questions.q: Which of the following elements has highest electronegativity?
questions.solution:
The electronegativity of elements decreases down a group in the periodic table. Given that all elements—beryllium, magnesium, calcium, and strontium—are alkaline earth metals in Group 2, beryllium, being highest in the group among these, exhibits the greatest electronegativity. Pauling scale values confirm this: $1.57$ for Be, $1.31$ for Mg, $1.00$ for Ca, and $0.95$ for Sr.

Final Answer: The answer is $\boxed{D}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Which is the correct increasing order of atomic radii of $\mathrm{Na}, \mathrm{K}, \mathrm{Mg}, \mathrm{Rb}$ ?
questions.solution:
Atomic radius is determined by the number of electron shells and effective nuclear charge.

Periodic trends: Atomic radius decreases across a period due to increasing nuclear charge while electron shells remain constant. Atomic radius increases down a group as additional electron shells are added, outweighing the shielding effect of inner electrons.

The relative positions are: $\mathrm{Na}$ (Group 1, Period 3), $\mathrm{K}$ (Group 1, Period 4), $\mathrm{Mg}$ (Group 2, Period 3), and $\mathrm{Rb}$ (Group 1, Period 5).

Within Period 3, $\mathrm{Mg}$ lies to the right of $\mathrm{Na}$, giving $\mathrm{Mg} < \mathrm{Na}$.
Down Group 1, atomic radius increases: $\mathrm{Na} < \mathrm{K} < \mathrm{Rb}$.

Combining these inequalities yields the correct order: $\mathrm{Mg} < \mathrm{Na} < \mathrm{K} < \mathrm{Rb}$.

Only option B matches this ordering, making it the correct choice.

The final answer is $\boxed{\text{B}}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q:
If four different elements $\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}, \mathrm{C}$ and D having electronic configuration as $A=[\mathrm{Ne}] 3 \mathrm{~s}^2 3 \mathrm{p}^4$, $\dot{B}=[\mathrm{Ne}] 3 \mathrm{~s}^2 3 \mathrm{p}^5, \mathrm{C}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 \mathrm{~d}^{10} 4 \mathrm{~s}^2 4 \mathrm{p}^4$ and $\mathrm{D}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 \mathrm{~d}^{10} 4 \mathrm{~s}^2 4 \mathrm{p}^5$.
Identify the element with largest atomic radius.
questions.solution:
Elements C and D belong to period 4 , while elements A and B are from period 3, therefore the former will be larger in size. The configuration of $C$ and $D$ is $4 \mathrm{~s}^2 4 \mathrm{p}^4$ and $4 \mathrm{~s}^2 4 \mathrm{p}^5$ respectively, therefore D lies to the right of C and would be smaller than C .
$\therefore \quad$ Element C will have the largest atomic radius.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: $Which from following elements has highest value of ionization enthalpy  \left(\Delta_1 \mathrm{H}_1\right) ?$
questions.solution:
The ionization enthalpy (I.E.) is highest for the inert gases. Therefore I.E of Ar and He will be higher than the halogens Cl and I.
Down the group, I.E decreases due to increase in the atomic size.
Therefore, ionization enthalpy of $\mathrm{He}>\mathrm{Ar}$. varies as: $\mathrm{I} < \mathrm{Cl}$ and $\mathrm{Ar} < \mathrm{He}$.
Across a period, I.E increases with increase in atomic number.
Therefore, I.E of Cl and Ar is in the order: $\mathrm{Cl} < \mathrm{Ar}$.
Hence, the correct increasing order of ionization enthalpy for the given elements is:
$\mathrm{I} < \mathrm{Cl} < \mathrm{Ar} < \mathrm{He}$
He has the highest I.E.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Which block element from following are known as transition elements?
questions.solution: Transition elements (also known as transition metals) are elements that have partially filled $d$ orbitals. IUPAC defines transition elements as an element having a $\mathrm{d}$ subshell that is partially filled with electrons, or an element that has the ability to form stable cations with an incompletely filled d orbital. In general, any element which corresponds to the d-block of the modern periodic table (which consists of groups 3-12) is considered to be a transition element.

questions.q: Which halogen has the highest value of negative electron gain enthalpy?
questions.solution:
The added electron goes to the bigger $n = 3$ is i.e., occupies larger region to space and the electron-electron repulsion is much less.
So, Chlorine has the highest value of negative electron gain enthalpy
